w: Swamishri attended a special assembly for volunteers who had offered their services during the 7-day festival. During his blessings he said, “... You are all very fortunate to have offered your services during this festival. Many have taken leave from work and postponed their work and businesses. God will be pleased upon you all. Since you were born in this holy pilgrim place you too have become holy. No matter how many prostrations we offer to you it will not suffice...”
Swamishri left Mahelav and performed the ground breaking ceremony of a new mandir in the nearby village of Padgol.
At 6.20 p.m. Swamishri attended an assembly in the village of Guntli.
At 6.40 p.m. Swamishri travelled to Sunav village and sanctified the land donated for a new Swaminarayan mandir.
Swamishri reached Bochasan at 7.40 p.m.

2000.o: Swamishri performed the Murti pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj at the Swaminarayan Mandir, Fulnagar
w: And also performed the Murti pratishtha of the murti of Ramdevpir at the Ramdevpir Mandir.
108 people pledged to refrain from addictions on the occasion of the Mandir opening and Swamishri's arrival.
Swamishri initiated 400 aspirants into Satsang during a mass initiation ceremony.
Swamishri flew in a small passenger plane from Pune to Surat, arriving at 11.45 am. After Thakorji’s darshan Swamishri had lunch at 12.55 pm.
In the evening satsang assembly 30,000 devotees and well-wishers welcomed Swamishri and listened to his blessings.

After 36 years Swamishri celebrated the festival of Vasant Panchmi in Gondal. This time Swamishri wished to celebrate the birthday celebration of Shastriji Maharaj in the precincts of Akshar Deri – the memorial shrine of Gunatitanand Swami. Swamishri had, prior to his arrival in Gondal, given instructions to organize the festival celebration on a grand scale.

Today, also marked the 140th pratishtha anniversary of Akshar Deri. Vasant Panchmi celebrates the birthdays of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, Brahmanand Swami, Nishkulanand Swami and the Shikshapatri. The celebration was held in front of the giant Akshar Dwar facing the mandir. The giant gate was decorated with flowers and lights; and the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and giant cutout figures of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj blessed the assembly. The assembly commenced with dhun and prayers at 5.00 pm. The assembly was themed on the contributions of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the birth and growth of the BAPS. An introduction to the theme was given by Apurvamuni Swami. This was followed by a mono-acting skit showing Chandubhai Vidya-dhikari’s glory for Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Thereafter Atmatrupt Swami talked about the service of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. This was followed by a traditional dance by children. Thereafter Brahmadarshan Swami elaborated upon Shastriji Maharaj’s indomitable faith in the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy. With Swamishri’s arrival at about 6.15 pm BAPS children waved flags from the balconies of Akshar Dwar and on terraces of the surrounding mandir buildings. Then a drama was presented by the youths of Gondal, depicting the deep impression that the then Shankracharya had for Shastriji Maharaj’s saintliness. Adarshjivan Swami spoke about Shastriji Maharaj’s saintliness and Siddheshwar Swami elaborated upon Yogiji Maharaj’s saintliness. Thereafter a short drama was enacted to show the diksha of Swamishri in Akshar Deri. Then, Viveksagar Swami spoke eloquently about the Gunatit Gurus and Swamishri’s glory and services in developing the BAPS. This was followed by an address from Balmukund Swami. Then the youths of Gondal performed a traditional dance during which a video of Shastriji Maharaj was shown. Finally, the celebration was crowned with Swamishri’s blessings, “The glory of this Sanstha is immense. The Akshar Deri was impossible to acquire, however with the divine powers of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj we got it and then this beautiful, miraculous place was built. The Akshar Deri fulfils the wishes of countless people.

“Shastriji Maharaj had firmly understood the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy. He researched and found references of the philosophy from the Sampraday’s shastras – Vachanamrut, Harililamrut and others. He also met the great sadgurus and, through their testimonies, confirmed the fact that Gunatitanand Swami is Mul Akshar and Sahajanand Swami is Purna Purushottam. The Bhagvad Gita speaks about Aksharbrahma yoga in the eighth chapter and Purushottam yoga in the fifteenth chapter. So, what he preached and established was not a willfully concocted philosophy or a consequence of a mere dream. He had confirmed and realized it himself. Despite all obstacles, Shastriji Maharaj had a single goal and faith that with Sahajanand Swami and Gunatitanand Swami with him nothing would happen to him. To believe and have faith that whatever God does will be for one’s good in challenging and turbulent situations is a great thing. “Shastriji Maharaj did not change the words of the Vachanamrut to prove his belief. Even today the content of the Vachanamrut copies printed are the same as they were. He has never done anything to increase his glory. He always talked about agna, upasana, sadbhav and paksh. Yogiji Maharaj preached samp, suhrudaybhav and ekta. God is pleased when one follows his agna and exercises paksh and sadbhav for his devotees.”
In conclusion, Swamishri and 12,000 devotees performed arti and thereafter took mahaprasad. The divine celebration in the precincts of Akshar Mandir left everyone spiritually elated and elevated.

Swamishri was offering food to Thakorji. Meanwhile Prabuddhamuni Swami and the pujari Mangaltirth Swami spoke of the plight of Indian students now studying in the UK, in London. Because of the British government's policies and because they cannot find jobs, students who went from India on loans are sleeping in car parks in the depths of winter. With no jobs, when they face starvation, they have to beg to eat. They gave some examples. They also said that, by your inspiration, every Saturday and Sunday at the mandir we feed all of them free, and we comfort everyone who comes with such pain and also try to help them find some work.
Swamishri was pleased and said, "Comforting them and feeding everyone is great work."

st.t: ‘Marvelous Complex to India’s History and Culture’: US Ambassador to India Kenneth Juster Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: The United States Ambassador to India, Mr.Kenneth I. Juster, visits Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. Sadhu Gnanmunidas welcomes US Ambassador Juster traditionally with tying a kalva (sacred thread). Ambassador Juster performs abhishek of Shri Neelkanth Varni at Swaminarayan Akshardham. United States Ambassador Kenneth Juster at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi.

United States Ambassador to India, Kenneth Juster, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham for the first time, signifying the decades-long tie between BAPS and the United States. Ambassador Juster was greeted by Sadhu Gnanmunidas in a traditional manner on behalf of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, the current spiritual leader of BAPS.

During Ambassador Juster’s visit, he offered respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy bodies of water from across India on the murti of Shri Neelkanth Varni. He also toured the educational Sanskruti Vihar, a cultural voyage that displays 10,000 years of India’s heritage and contributions to society.
“Thank you for a wonderful tour of the fabulous Akshardham Temple. This is a marvelous complex and provides a good overview of India’s history and culture, ” Ambassador Juster said.

Ambassador Juster’s visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham continues a long tradition of BAPS’ friendship with the United States, where there are five traditional shikarbadh mandirs and over 100 centers and hari mandirs. Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the fifth spiritual leader of BAPS, first visited America in 1974, returning nearly 15 times and traveling across the country. Since then, BAPS’ presence in America has continued to grow and flourish with an emphasis on community service and charity under the guidance of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, who most recently visited the United States in 2017.
